AXES.sub: What the surrogate is fitted on
After the loop ends, how the fitted surrogate is turned into one number P̂f. Independent of which points were chosen — same design, different readout, different answer.
AXES.eff: A9→A11 is a pure readout effect: −11.80 points

AXES.sub: Where the width w comes from
AXES.eff: CQR is a no-op unless observations are corrupted

How the candidate population is drawn

What the surrogate is asked to represent

opts.m: one surrogate on the min · all arms

A1.d: GP surrogate, sign-ambiguity acquisition, one point per iteration over the full population. This is AK-MCS with a fixed budget instead of a stopping rule.

A2.d: A1 with UCB exploration: σ × ambiguity. Isolates exploration from calibration.

A3.d: Same GP mean; the width becomes a distribution-free jackknife interval scaled by nearest-neighbour distance.

A4.d: XGBoost replaces the GP mean. Data-hungry — blocky on 12-62 points.

A5.d: TabICL foundation model + K-fold conformal width. First arm under 1% on the smooth truss suite.

A7.d: A5 with TabICL's own native band instead of the conformal width. Isolates what conformal calibration adds.

A8.d: Underflow-free sign-ambiguity (s = σ/|μ|) on the native band. Best margin-target arm on the truss suite.

A9.d: CQR band keeps TabICL's input-dependent band shape and adds a conformal offset Q_c for coverage.

A10.d: A8 × A9 hybrid: sign-ambiguity form, CQR band as σ.

A11.d: A9's design with the readout surrogate fitted on T(g) = g/(1+|g|). The robust margin-target arm wherever the compression acts.

A12.d: A8's acquisition with A11's compressed target. Verdict: does not work. The compression is a pairing with the CQR design, not a portable fix.

EFF+CQR.d: Best arm measured anywhere in this project: 1.1 ± 1.2%. Capacity-side β target, EFF with a conformal offset, Rao-Blackwellised readout.

EFF-RB.d: Same as EFF+CQR without the conformal offset — 1.3 ± 0.8%. On clean data the offset is a no-op, so these two are statistically indistinguishable.

A12-rand.d: A random 300-point design. 1.8 ± 1.1% — ties EFF and beats the U-function. The single most informative arm in the project: it prices what active learning is actually buying at this target.

A8-RB.d: U-function acquisition on the β target with RB readout — 2.5 ± 1.9%. Worse than random.

A12-pc.d: Probability-band-width acquisition on the β target — 2.7 ± 1.7%. A different method from the A12 above — two unrelated things carry that name here.

AK-MCS-C2.d: AK-MCS wrapped in conformal prediction. Instead of thresholding a learning function, the loop terminates when a distribution-free conformal interval on Pf reaches a target tightness, giving a certified bound at a user-chosen coverage level rather than a point estimate. This closes the conformal-coverage stopping cell, which was marked open on this page until 2026 — and it sits directly on top of this project’s own line of work.
AK-MCS-C2.r: Jaber, Chabridon & Mougeot, “AK-MCS-C2: active Kriging Monte Carlo simulation method with conformal certification for failure probability estimation”, arXiv 2606.20191, 19 June 2026. Code: github.com/EdgarJaber/AK-MCS-C2. Checked — preprint, not yet a journal version.

MFIS.d: Multifidelity importance sampling: a cheap surrogate is used only to construct the biasing density, and every weight in the estimator is evaluated with the high-fidelity model — so surrogate error costs variance, never bias. The cleanest statement of the argument I gave you for fitting a proposal on a surrogate. Verified citation.
MFIS.r: Peherstorfer, Cui, Marzouk & Willcox, “Multifidelity importance sampling”, CMAME 300, 490-509, 2016 (doi 10.1016/j.cma.2015.12.002).

NN-SuS.d: Neural-network surrogates accelerating each conditional level of subset simulation — an early demonstration that the expensive part of SuS is the per-level model calls, not the MCMC.

AK-Gibbs.d: Active-learning Kriging driven by a Gibbs importance-sampling sampler, aimed specifically at small failure probabilities with non-linear, high-dimensional limit states — the regime where a single-shot proposal degenerates.

AK-truncCR.d: Restricts the candidate pool to a truncated region around the current boundary estimate instead of scoring the whole population — the principled version of a random candidate subsample, and applied to system reliability with several components.
AK-truncCR.r: Yang, Liu, Mi and co-authors, RESS 169, 235-241, 2018. Verified — authors found and year corrected from an earlier guess of 2016/2017.

MF-CE.d: Multifidelity preconditioning of the cross-entropy method: a hierarchy of cheap surrogates does the expensive part — iterating the tempered CE fit to locate the biasing density — and the high-fidelity model is reserved for the final estimator. Reported speedups of several orders of magnitude over single-fidelity CE. This is the direct answer to running CE-IS on a surrogate. Verified citation.
MF-CE.r: Peherstorfer, Kramer & Willcox, SIAM/ASA J. Uncertainty Quantification 6(2), 737-761, 2018.

DIS-TT.d: Approximates the optimal IS density as the pushforward of a reference under a composition of order-preserving maps built from squared tensor-train decompositions. The non-neural competitor to REIN: same goal, functional approximation instead of a network, and it handles multimodal densities concentrated in the tails. Verified citation.
DIS-TT.r: Cui, Dolgov & Scheichl, SIAM J. Scientific Computing 46(1), C1-C29, 2024; foundations in Cui & Dolgov, Found. Comput. Math. 22(6), 1863-1922, 2022.

MF-failprob.d: Combines an arbitrary number of surrogates of any type — coarse meshes, reduced-order models, data-fit metamodels — into one unbiased failure-probability estimator, with the high-fidelity model called only where the cheap ones disagree. The named occupant of the reduced-order fidelity cell, and the last dark cell on this page. Verified citation.
MF-failprob.r: Peherstorfer, Kramer & Willcox, “Combining multiple surrogate models to accelerate failure probability estimation with expensive high-fidelity models”, J. Computational Physics 341, 61-75, 2017.

REIF.d: Reliability-based expected improvement, derived from the folded-normal distribution of |g| under the Kriging posterior — so the criterion is an expected improvement toward the limit state rather than a distance-to-boundary heuristic like U or a feasibility integral like EFF. REIF2 additionally modulates by the input joint density, which is the correction your own IS discussion would demand. Verified citation.
REIF.r: Zhang, Wang & Sørensen, “REIF: a novel active-learning function toward adaptive Kriging surrogate models for structural reliability analysis”, RESS 185, 440-454, 2019.

SubSim-Bayes.d: A Bayesian post-processor for subset simulation: instead of a point estimate, Pf gets a full posterior from the conditional-level counts, plus MCMC enhancements aimed squarely at high dimensions. The honest answer to “what is the uncertainty on my subset-simulation number”. Verified citation.

EDSD.d: Explicit design space decomposition: an SVM builds an explicit analytical boundary between safe and failed, updated by three geometric rules — a sample at a set distance from the nearest training point, one at maximum distance from the last added, and one at maximum-minimum distance from all existing. Purely geometric enrichment, no probabilistic model. Verified citation.

AK-SVR.d: Adaptive support-vector regression inside subset simulation — a margin-regressing SVM rather than 2SMART’s classifier, so the conditional levels get a continuous surrogate. Reaches very small Pf without a Gaussian process.

Perrin-multimode.d: Active-learning surrogates built for systems with several failure modes at once, refining whichever mode governs at each candidate rather than the composed minimum. An independent route to the same place as AK-SYS.

AK-stratIS.d: Stratified importance sampling driven by an adaptive Kriging model: the sample budget is allocated across strata by their contribution to the variance of P̂<sub>f</sub>, with the surrogate deciding which strata matter. The named occupant of the stratified cell.
AK-stratIS.r: Xiao, Oladyshkin & Nowak, RESS 197, 2020 (doi 10.1016/j.ress.2020.106852). Verified — authors corrected, previously misattributed here to “Xiao, Zhan & Shi”.

LHS-reliability.d: The systematic study of Latin hypercube and stratified designs for reliability specifically — where variance reduction actually materialises in the tail and where it does not. The foundational anchor for that cell.

AK-multiregion.d: An adaptive-Kriging importance technique built specifically for limit states whose failure domain splits into several low-probability regions, which a single design-point proposal silently misses.

AK-SS-explore.d: Kriging inside subset simulation with an acquisition that explicitly balances exploration of the failure region against exploitation of the current boundary estimate — the closest published relative of your UCB arms.

ASS-seq.d: A sequential sampling scheme that adapts both where and how many points to add per iteration, judged against an accuracy measure of the surrogate rather than a fixed budget.

Kriging-accuracy.d: Two accuracy measures for the Kriging model in reliability analysis — an attempt to say how wrong P̂<sub>f</sub> can be given the current surrogate, rather than thresholding a learning function. Same problem REAK and ESC attack.
Kriging-accuracy.r: Wang, Sun, Yang & Li, RESS 167, 494-505, 2017. Verified — authors corrected; previously listed here as “Jian, Zhu, Liang”, a mis-parse of the lead author’s given name.

parallel-SUR.d: Fast parallel stepwise uncertainty reduction: selects a whole batch by the expected joint reduction in excursion-set uncertainty, with the closed forms that make it computable. The principled version of batch selection your local-penalisation heuristic approximates.
parallel-SUR.r: Chevalier, Bect, Ginsbourger, Vazquez, Picheny & Richet, Technometrics 56(4), 455-465, 2014. Verified.

RSM-1990.d: The origin of the whole idea: replace the finite-element model with a quadratic response surface fitted near the design point, then run FORM or sampling on the cheap surface. Every surrogate reliability method descends from this.
RSM-1990.r: Bucher & Bourgund, “A fast and efficient response surface approach for structural reliability problems”, Structural Safety 7(1), 1990.

CQ2RS.d: A statistical reworking of the response-surface method that treats the fitted surface as uncertain and uses that uncertainty to place the next experiments — an active-learning idea a decade before AK-MCS, from the same Clermont group.

IS-highdim.d: The paper behind the caveat that importance sampling is not automatically dead in high dimensions: a pure mean-shift to the design point degrades gracefully, whereas scaling the proposal covariance is what makes the weights collapse as d grows.
IS-highdim.r: Au & Beck, Structural Safety 25(2), 139-163, 2003. Verified. The geometric counterpart is Katafygiotis & Zuev, Prob. Eng. Mechanics, 2008.

ARBIS.d: Adaptive radial-based importance sampling: samples in a growing spherical annulus in standard normal space, adapting the inner radius, instead of centring on one MPP. The origin of the AK-ARBIS family.

multi-MPP.d: Systematic location of multiple design points by barrier-constrained re-solves, so an IS proposal can cover several disjoint failure regions instead of the one FORM happens to find first.

adv-LS.d: Advanced line sampling: adapts the important direction as lines are drawn and reuses roots between lines, which is what makes line sampling competitive rather than merely elegant.

meta-LS.d: Line sampling where a Kriging model supplies the root along each line instead of a bisection on the true model — the surrogate is asked for a 1-D root, not a full boundary.

SKRA-par.d: Sequential Kriging reliability with adaptive sampling regions: restricts candidates to a shrinking region around the boundary and draws a whole batch from it per iteration, so the expensive model can be run in parallel. The named occupant of the parallel-regions cell.
SKRA-par.r: Wen, Pei, Liu & Yue, RESS 153, 170-179, 2016 (doi 10.1016/j.ress.2016.05.002). Verified — authors corrected, previously misattributed here to “Wen, Jia & Zhou”.

seq-LDR.d: Learns a low-dimensional linear subspace and the reliability surrogate together, refining the projection as points arrive rather than fixing it up front. The most direct published answer to a 50-RV wall.
seq-LDR.r: Ehre, Papaioannou, Sudret & Straub, SIAM J. Scientific Computing 44, B558-B584, 2022. Verified — and it is PLS-PCE driven, not an active subspace, so it sits on the PLS cell.

SubSim.d: Subset simulation itself — the failure event is factored into a chain of nested, more probable conditional events sampled by MCMC. Not a surrogate method; it is the population strategy every later AL+SS hybrid sits on top of. 2001, so it predates the window, but it is the origin of that cell.
SubSim.r: Au & Beck, Probabilistic Engineering Mechanics 16(4), 2001. The conditional MCMC kernel is itself a live sub-question: Papaioannou, Betz, Zwirglmaier & Straub, “MCMC algorithms for subset simulation”, PEM 41, 89-103, 2015 (verified), compare modified-Metropolis variants and show the kernel governs performance as dimension grows.

CE-method.d: The cross-entropy method: fit a parametric proposal by minimising KL divergence to the zero-variance density, iterating through tempered intermediate events. Origin of the CE-IS cell; 1997-2004, before the window.
CE-method.r: Rubinstein, 1997/1999; tutorial by de Boer, Kroese, Mannor & Rubinstein, Annals of OR, 2005.

Ranjan-contour.d: Sequential design for contour estimation from expensive codes — the first criterion to target a level set rather than a global fit. The direct conceptual ancestor of EFF and the U-function.

tIMSE.d: Targeted integrated mean-square error: weights the IMSE by how close a point is to the target region, so the design refines the boundary rather than the whole domain. An early variance-reduction acquisition, not a margin heuristic.
tIMSE.r: Picheny, Ginsbourger, Roustant, Haftka & Kim, J. Mechanical Design 132(7), 071008, 2010. Verified.

SUR-Bect.d: Stepwise uncertainty reduction: choose the point that most reduces the expected posterior variance of Pf itself, rather than a proxy for boundary proximity. This is the SUR your run_acq_variants.py implements and cites — where it cost 9× and gained nothing.
SUR-Bect.r: Bect, Ginsbourger, Li, Picheny & Vazquez, Statistics and Computing 22, 2012.

2SMART.d: Support-vector classification driven inside subset simulation, with the margin used to place new points at each conditional level. One of the earliest AL methods to reach very small P<sub>f</sub>, and an SVM answer rather than a Kriging one.

sparse-PCE.d: Sparse polynomial chaos by least-angle regression — selects the few basis terms that matter instead of a full tensor expansion, which is what made PCE viable in more than a handful of dimensions.
sparse-PCE.r: Blatman & Sudret, J. Computational Physics 230, 2011; Prob. Eng. Mech. 25, 2010.

AK-SYS.d: Adapts AK-MCS to system reliability: one Kriging model per component, and the learning function is evaluated on the composed system event rather than a single margin. Refines only the component that governs at each candidate.
AK-SYS.r: Fauriat & Gayton, RESS 123, 137-144, 2014 (doi 10.1016/j.ress.2013.10.010). Verified. Successor: AK-SYSi with a refined U function, SMO, 2018.

EGRA-sys.d: The EGRA counterpart for multiple failure modes — surrogates each mode and composes, with the expected feasibility evaluated against the system limit state.

Kriging-AIS.d: Kriging-based adaptive importance sampling: the proposal is refitted as the surrogate improves, with explicit provision for several disjoint failure regions rather than one design point.

SIS.d: Sequential importance sampling: a chain of tempered intermediate densities driven by MCMC, with the estimator accumulated across levels. The non-parametric alternative to fitting a CE family, and the direct competitor to subset simulation.

BSS.d: Bayesian subset simulation — puts a GP prior on the limit state and runs subset simulation under the posterior, choosing points to reduce the posterior uncertainty of each conditional probability. The earliest anchor for the Bayesian-quadrature cells.
BSS.r: Bect, Li & Vazquez, SIAM/ASA J. Uncertainty Quantification 5(1), 762-786, 2017. Verified.

APCE-boot.d: Sparse polynomial chaos with bootstrap replications supplying the epistemic band, so a PCE gets a usable local error estimate without a GP posterior. This is the named occupant of the bootstrap UQ cell.

SVM-MCS.d: Adaptive support-vector classification of the failure domain rather than regression of the margin — the surrogate learns the boundary directly, which suits discontinuous and highly non-linear limit states.

mfEGRA.d: Multi-fidelity EGRA: acquires both the location and the fidelity level, spending most calls on the cheap model and reserving the expensive one for points near the boundary. The named occupant of the multi-fidelity cell.
mfEGRA.r: Chaudhuri, Marques & Willcox, Struct. & Multidisc. Optimization 64(2), 2021. Verified (year corrected from 2020). Two-stage criterion: EGRA’s expected feasibility plus a one-step-lookahead information gain that also picks the fidelity.

KPLS-AK.d: Kriging built on partial-least-squares components instead of the raw inputs, which keeps hyperparameter fitting tractable as the dimension grows. A cheap, generic answer to the axis your 50-RV benchmark dies on.
KPLS-AK.r: Bouhlel, Bartoli, Otsmane & Morlier, Struct. & Multidisc. Optimization 53(5), 935-952, 2016. Verified.

DNN-AL.d: Deep network surrogate with weighted resampling in the learning loop. Needs far more points than a GP, so it earns its place only on problems where the limit state is genuinely high-dimensional or non-smooth.
DNN-AL.r: Xiang, Chen, Bao and co-authors, Mechanical Systems & Signal Processing 140, 106684, 2020. Verified.

AK-ARBIS.d: Kriging placed inside Grooteman’s radial scheme, so the surrogate only has to be accurate within the current annulus. Keeps working when the failure domain is not concentrated near one MPP.
AK-ARBIS.r: Yun, Lu, Jiang, Zhang & He, “AK-ARBIS: an improved AK-MCS based on the adaptive radial-based importance sampling for small failure probability”, Structural Safety 82, 101891, 2020. Verified.

AK-MCS.d: The canonical method. Kriging + crude MCS, U-function, one point per iteration, stop when min U ≥ 2.

EGRA.d: Expected feasibility instead of U. Predates AK-MCS and is still the main alternative learning function.
EGRA.r: Bichon, Eldred, Swiler, Mahadevan & McFarland, AIAA Journal 46(10), 2008.

AK-IS.d: AK-MCS with a FORM design-point IS density and a weighted estimator. The direct ancestor of combining AL with importance sampling.
AK-IS.r: Echard, Gayton, Lemaire & Relun, Rel. Eng. & System Safety 111, 2013.

meta-IS.d: Builds the proposal from the surrogate's own epistemic uncertainty — self-defensive by construction, since it keeps mass where the model is unsure.
meta-IS.r: Dubourg, Sudret & Deheeger, Prob. Eng. Mechanics 33, 2013; extended to reliability sensitivities in Structural Safety 49, 2014.

AK-SS.d: AK-MCS inside subset simulation's nested intermediate failure events. The standard route to Pf ≤ 1e-4.
AK-SS.r: Huang, Chen & Zhu, Structural Safety 59, 86-95, 2016 (doi 10.1016/j.strusafe.2015.12.003). Verified. The family stayed active: “Efficient subset simulation with active learning Kriging model for low failure probability prediction”, PEM 69, 2022 (venue verified, authors unchecked), and a coupled SuS/AK variant in SMO, 2019.

APCK-MCS.d: Polynomial-chaos Kriging — a PCE trend with a Kriging residual — under the same AL loop.
APCK-MCS.r: Schöbi, Sudret & Marelli, ASCE-ASME J. Risk Uncertainty, 2017; the PC-Kriging surrogate itself is Schöbi, Sudret & Wiart, IJUQ 5(2), 2015.

AK-MCSi.d: Batch AK-MCS: take the U < 2 pool, k-means it into clusters, evaluate the lowest-U member of each. Diversity by clustering instead of local penalisation.

REAK.d: Replaces the min-U heuristic with a bound on the error rate of the estimated Pf, so the loop stops when the probability of misclassifying the population is provably small. The direct answer to the pinned stopping axis.
REAK.r: Wang & Shafieezadeh, RESS 182, 33-45, 2019. Verified. Companion error-based stopping criterion (ESC) by the same authors, SMO, 2019.

PAB-BQ.d: Bayesian quadrature: Pf is treated as a random variable with a posterior, and points are acquired in parallel to shrink its variance. Gives a credible interval on Pf rather than a point estimate.

BAL-LS.d: The same Bayesian formulation applied along lines rather than over a population — line sampling with an actively learned root distribution.
BAL-LS.r: Dang, Valdebenito, Faes, Song, Wei & Beer, “Structural reliability analysis by line sampling: a Bayesian active learning treatment”, Structural Safety 104, 102351, 2023. Verified. Companions: partially-Bayesian ALLS in CMAME, 2023, and a log-normal-process variant in RESS 246, 2024.

FIDR-CE.d: Cross-entropy IS where the proposal is fitted only in a low-dimensional failure-informed subspace, which is what keeps CE-IS alive as the dimension grows. The obvious lever for the 50-RV collapse.
FIDR-CE.r: Uribe, Papaioannou, Marzouk & Straub, SIAM/ASA J. Uncertainty Quantification 9, 818-847, 2021. Verified.

MF-AK.d: Co-Kriging over a cheap and an expensive model, acquiring both the point and the fidelity level. Reported FE savings come from spending most calls on the coarse model.
MF-AK.r: “An active-learning method based on multi-fidelity Kriging model for structural reliability analysis”, Struct. & Multidisc. Optimization, 2020 (doi 10.1007/s00158-020-02678-1). Venue verified; the canonical multi-fidelity entry on this page is mfEGRA.

REIN.d: A normalizing flow learns a map from the input distribution to a quasi-optimal IS density directly — stacked invertible networks with cheap Jacobian determinants, so the proposal is trained rather than fitted from a parametric family. The concrete answer to “can a flow replace the CE mixture”. Verified citation.
REIN.r: Dasgupta & Johnson, “REIN: reliability estimation via importance sampling with normalizing flows”, RESS 242, 2024 (doi 10.1016/j.ress.2023.109729). Related: NOFIS, which learns a sequence of proposals over nested subset events.

TabPFN-AL.d: Tabular foundation models as the surrogate — in-context learning replaces per-problem fitting, which is what makes the 12-62 point regime workable. This is the family A5-A12 belong to.
TabPFN-AL.r: Tabular foundation model — Hollmann et al., Nature, 2025 (TabPFN v2). TabICL is a sibling architecture.
